nodes.name: file-reclaim.test.mjs
nodes.body_text: /** * Local mirror of the hub's scalar-file-column ratchet. * * Every column holding a hub file id must be named by * `manifest.delete_file_columns`, so the hub reads the id off the doomed row * and queues the R2 reclaim inside the DELETE's own transaction. The pattern * this replaces was a trailing `files.delete(id).catch(() => {})` in the * client, fired after the row was already gone: when it was interrupted the * metadata row survived, so the orphan reconciler read the object as live, no * UI could reach it, and it stayed billed against the household's hard file cap * until the app was uninstalled. * * `delete_cascades` does NOT satisfy this. That key fires when the PARENT is * deleted; a direct DELETE of the row that owns the file consults * `delete_file_columns` and nothing else. * * The hub rejects the bundle at publish time. This test is the same check where * it is cheap to fix. */ import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest"; import { manifest, prefix, appTableColumns } from "./schema.mjs"; /** Scalar hub-file-id columns. List columns (`*_file_ids`) are a different * lane — the reclaim engine reads raw SQL and cannot parse a JSON array. */ const FILE_ID_COLUMN_RE = /^(?:file_id|file_key|photo_id|[a-z0-9_]*_file_id|[a-z0-9_]*_photo_id|[a-z0-9_]*_image_id)$/; /** [unprefixedTable, column] for every scalar file column in the schema. */ /** Tables/columns whose deletes reclaim durably: delete_file_columns, plus * versioned_records (that lane reclaims through the countersigned purge). */ describe("hub file reclaim", () => { it("declares every scalar file column for the app-originated delete lane", () => { const declared = declaredColumns(); const undeclared = schemaFileColumns() .filter(([table, column]) => !declared.get(table)?.has(column)) .map(([table, column]) => `${table}.${column}`); expect(undeclared).toEqual([]); }); it("names only real tables and columns", () => { const tables = appTableColumns(); for (const [table, columns] of Object.entries(manifest.delete_file_columns ?? {})) { const names = tables.get(`${prefix}${table}`); expect(names, `delete_file_columns.${table} has no CREATE TABLE`).toBeDefined(); // The engine resolves the doomed rows by id before deleting them. expect(names.has("id"), `${table} needs an id column`).toBe(true); for (const column of columns) { expect(names.has(column), `${table}.${column} is missing from the schema`).toBe(true); // The reclaim reads this column in raw SQL, outside the decrypt path. expect(column.endsWith("_id") || (manifest.db_plaintext_columns ?? []).includes(column) || manifest.db_encryption === "off", `${table}.${column} would be encrypted at rest`).toBe(true); } } }); });

nodes.name: schemaFileColumns
nodes.body_text: function schemaFileColumns() { const found = []; for (const [physical, columns] of appTableColumns()) { for (const column of columns) { if (FILE_ID_COLUMN_RE.test(column)) found.push([physical.slice(prefix.length), column]); } } return found; }

nodes.name: declaredColumns
nodes.body_text: function declaredColumns() { const declared = new Map(); const add = (table, columns) => { if (!table) return; const set = declared.get(table) ?? new Set(); declared.set(table, set); for (const column of [columns].flat().filter(Boolean)) set.add(column); }; for (const [table, columns] of Object.entries(manifest.delete_file_columns ?? {})) add(table, columns); for (const cfg of Object.values(manifest.versioned_records ?? {})) { add(cfg.table, cfg.file_column); add(cfg.version_table, cfg.file_column); } return declared; }

nodes.body_text: import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest"; import { canEdit, parseIds, toggleId, liveIds, nameKey, findByName, tagsOf, searchableFields, filterItems, countByLabel, photosOf, coverPhoto, collectionCover, cutoutState, canRequestCutout, showsCutout, displayFileId, cutoutFailure, cutoutLabel, fitWithin, thumbName, plural, cleanDate, formatDate, withoutDeleted, pendingElsewhere, needsCheck, holdKey, holdIsFresh, HOLD_FRESH_MS, PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS, } from "../src/logic.js"; const adult = { id: "a", role: "adult" }; const admin = { id: "z", role: "admin" }; const kid = { id: "k", role: "child" }; describe("canEdit", () => { it("lets the member who added a row, and any adult, change it", () => { expect(canEdit({ created_by: "k" }, kid)).toBe(true); expect(canEdit({ created_by: "k" }, adult)).toBe(true); expect(canEdit({ created_by: "k" }, admin)).toBe(true); }); it("refuses another child, a missing row and a missing member", () => { expect(canEdit({ created_by: "a" }, kid)).toBe(false); expect(canEdit(null, adult)).toBe(false); expect(canEdit({ created_by: "k" }, null)).toBe(false); }); }); describe("ids stored on an item", () => { it("reads a JSON array and nothing else", () => { expect(parseIds(`["a","b"]`)).toEqual(["a", "b"]); expect(parseIds(["a", 3, "b"])).toEqual(["a", "b"]); for (const bad of ["", null, undefined, "not json", `{"a":1}`, `"a"`, 7]) expect(parseIds(bad)).toEqual([]); expect(parseIds(`["a",1,null]`)).toEqual(["a"]); }); it("toggles without touching the list it was given", () => { const ids = ["a"]; expect(toggleId(ids, "b")).toEqual(["a", "b"]); expect(toggleId(ids, "a")).toEqual([]); expect(ids).toEqual(["a"]); }); it("drops ids whose tag is gone", () => { expect(liveIds(["a", "gone", "b"], [{ id: "a" }, { id: "b" }])).toEqual(["a", "b"]); }); }); describe("names", () => { it("treats case and spacing as the same name", () => { expect(nameKey(" Bin 1 ")).toBe("bin 1"); const rows = [{ id: "1", name: "Garage" }]; expect(findByName(rows, " garage ")).toBe(rows[0]); expect(findByName(rows, "Attic")).toBeNull(); expect(findByName([{ id: "x", name: "" }], " ")).toBeNull(); }); it("keeps tags to their own collection", () => { const tags = [{ id: "1", collection_id: "c1" }, { id: "2", collection_id: "c2" }]; expect(tagsOf(tags, "c1")).toEqual([tags[0]]); }); }); describe("finding items", () => { const items = [ { id: "1", collection_id: "c1", name: "Barnaby", note: "From Grandma", tag_ids: `["steiff","gift"]`, location_ids: `["shelf"]` }, { id: "2", collection_id: "c1", name: "Honey", note: "", tag_ids: `["gift"]`, location_ids: `["bin"]` }, { id: "3", collection_id: "c2", name: "Drill", note: "", tag_ids: "", location_ids: `["bin","garage"]` }, ]; it("is findable by note, tag name and place name, not just its name", () => { const names = new Map([["steiff", "Steiff"], ["shelf", "Bedroom shelf"]]); const fields = searchableFields(items[0], names); expect(fields).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(["Barnaby", "From Grandma", "Steiff", "Bedroom shelf"])); // A tag whose name is unknown adds nothing, and no map is needed at all. expect(fields).toHaveLength(4); expect(searchableFields(items[2])).toEqual(["Drill", ""]); }); it("narrows to one collection", () => { expect(ids(filterItems(items, { collectionId: "c1" }))).toEqual(["1", "2"]); expect(ids(filterItems(items))).toEqual(["1", "2", "3"]); }); it("needs every chosen tag", () => { expect(ids(filterItems(items, { tagIds: ["gift"] }))).toEqual(["1", "2"]); expect(ids(filterItems(items, { tagIds: ["gift", "steiff"] }))).toEqual(["1"]); }); it("needs any one chosen place", () => { expect(ids(filterItems(items, { locationIds: ["bin"] }))).toEqual(["2", "3"]); expect(ids(filterItems(items, { locationIds: ["shelf", "garage"] }))).toEqual(["1", "3"]); expect(ids(filterItems(items, { collectionId: "c1", locationIds: ["bin"], tagIds: ["gift"] }))).toEqual(["2"]); }); it("counts items per tag and per place", () => { expect(countByLabel(items, "tag_ids")).toEqual(new Map([["steiff", 1], ["gift", 2]])); expect(countByLabel(items, "location_ids").get("bin")).toBe(2); }); }); describe("photos of an item", () => { const photos = [ { id: "b", item_id: "1", sort_order: 1, created_at: "2026-01-02" }, { id: "a", item_id: "1", sort_order: 0, created_at: "2026-01-03" }, { id: "c", item_id: "1", sort_order: 1, created_at: "2026-01-01" }, { id: "d", item_id: "2", sort_order: 0, created_at: "2026-01-01" }, ]; it("orders by position, then oldest first", () => { expect(photosOf(photos, "1").map((photo) => photo.id)).toEqual(["a", "c", "b"]); expect(coverPhoto(photos, "1").id).toBe("a"); expect(coverPhoto(photos, "none")).toBeNull(); }); it("covers a collection with its newest item that has a photo", () => { const items = [{ id: "9", collection_id: "c1" }, { id: "2", collection_id: "c1" }, { id: "1", collection_id: "c1" }, { id: "x", collection_id: "c2" }]; expect(collectionCover(items, photos, "c1").id).toBe("d"); expect(collectionCover(items, photos, "c2")).toBeNull(); }); }); describe("where a cutout stands", () => { const now = Date.parse("2026-01-02T10:10:00Z"); it("is done whenever the row holds a cutout, whatever the status says", () => { expect(cutoutState({ cutout_file_id: "f", cutout_status: "pending" }, now)).toBe("done"); }); it("believes a pending row only while it is fresh", () => { expect(cutoutState({ cutout_status: "pending", cutout_requested_at: asked(PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS - 1) }, now)).toBe("pending"); expect(cutoutState({ cutout_status: "pending", cutout_requested_at: asked(PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS) }, now)).toBe("failed"); expect(cutoutState({ cutout_status: "pending", cutout_requested_at: null }, now)).toBe("failed"); expect(cutoutState({ cutout_status: "pending", cutout_requested_at: "garbage" }, now)).toBe("failed"); }); it("reads done-without-a-file as failed and an unknown status as none", () => { expect(cutoutState({ cutout_status: "done", cutout_file_id: null }, now)).toBe("failed"); expect(cutoutState({ cutout_status: "wat" }, now)).toBe("none"); expect(cutoutState({}, now)).toBe("none"); for (const status of ["none", "failed", "quota"]) expect(cutoutState({ cutout_status: status }, now)).toBe(status); }); it("never asks again for a photo that has a cutout or is waiting for one", () => { expect(canRequestCutout({ cutout_file_id: "f", cutout_status: "done" }, now)).toBe(false); expect(canRequestCutout({ cutout_status: "pending", cutout_requested_at: asked(1000) }, now)).toBe(false); expect(canRequestCutout({ cutout_status: "pending", cutout_requested_at: asked(PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS + 1) }, now)).toBe(true); for (const status of ["none", "failed", "quota"]) expect(canRequestCutout({ cutout_status: status }, now)).toBe(true); }); }); describe("a hold on a cutout request", () => { const now = Date.parse("2026-01-02T10:10:00Z"); it("needs no renewing while it is far too young for anyone else to take", () => { expect(holdIsFresh(taken(0), now)).toBe(true); expect(holdIsFresh(taken(HOLD_FRESH_MS - 1), now)).toBe(true); expect(holdIsFresh(taken(HOLD_FRESH_MS), now)).toBe(false); // Fresh must end well before another requester may take the row. expect(HOLD_FRESH_MS * 2).toBeLessThanOrEqual(PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS); }); it("is renewed when its age cannot be trusted", () => { for (const bad of [null, undefined, "", "garbage", taken(-5000)]) expect(holdIsFresh(bad, now)).toBe(false); }); }); describe("which file is drawn", () => { const photo = { file_id: "orig", thumb_file_id: "thumb", cutout_file_id: "cut", use_cutout: 1 }; it("draws the cutout when there is one and it is switched on", () => { expect(showsCutout(photo)).toBe(true); expect(displayFileId(photo)).toBe("cut"); expect(displayFileId(photo, { small: true })).toBe("cut"); }); it("draws the photo as taken when the cutout is switched off or absent", () => { expect(showsCutout({ ...photo, use_cutout: 0 })).toBe(false); expect(showsCutout({ ...photo, use_cutout: "0" })).toBe(false); expect(displayFileId({ ...photo, use_cutout: 0 })).toBe("orig"); expect(displayFileId({ ...photo, use_cutout: 0 }, { small: true })).toBe("thumb"); expect(displayFileId({ ...photo, cutout_file_id: null }, { small: true })).toBe("thumb"); expect(displayFileId({ file_id: "orig", thumb_file_id: null }, { small: true })).toBe("orig"); }); }); describe("a refused cutout", () => { it("tells the monthly allowance apart from the per-minute limit", () => { const spent = cutoutFailure(429, { error: "used up", used: 100, limit: 100 }); expect(spent).toMatchObject({ status: "quota", stop: true }); expect(spent.message).toContain("100"); expect(cutoutFailure(429, { error: "Too many requests" })).toEqual({ status: "failed", stop: false, message: "" }); expect(cutoutFailure(429, null).status).toBe("failed"); }); it("leaves the photo unasked when the household or the app may not have cutouts", () => { expect(cutoutFailure(402)).toMatchObject({ status: "none", stop: true }); expect(cutoutFailure(402).message).toMatch(/plan/); expect(cutoutFailure(403)).toEqual({ status: "none", stop: true, message: "" }); }); it("stops asking while the service is unavailable, and keeps going after one bad photo", () => { expect(cutoutFailure(503)).toMatchObject({ status: "failed", stop: true }); expect(cutoutFailure(502)).toEqual({ status: "failed", stop: false, message: "" }); expect(cutoutFailure(415).stop).toBe(false); expect(cutoutFailure(413).message).toMatch(/too large/); expect(cutoutFailure(undefined)).toEqual({ status: "failed", stop: false, message: "" }); }); it("has a line for each state worth explaining", () => { for (const state of ["pending", "failed", "quota"]) expect(cutoutLabel(state)).not.toBe(""); for (const state of ["none", "done"]) expect(cutoutLabel(state)).toBe(""); }); }); describe("images", () => { it("shrinks to the longest side and never enlarges", () => { expect(fitWithin(4000, 3000, 480)).toEqual({ width: 480, height: 360, scaled: true }); expect(fitWithin(3000, 4000, 480)).toEqual({ width: 360, height: 480, scaled: true }); expect(fitWithin(480, 300, 480)).toEqual({ width: 480, height: 300, scaled: false }); expect(fitWithin(0, 0, 480).scaled).toBe(false); }); it("names a thumbnail from the photo, safely", () => { expect(thumbName("IMG_0042.HEIC")).toBe("thumb-IMG_0042.jpg"); expect(thumbName("../../etc/pass<wd>.png")).toBe("thumb-etcpasswd.jpg"); expect(thumbName("")).toBe("thumb-photo.jpg"); expect(thumbName("x".repeat(200) + ".jpg").length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(70); }); }); describe("a page that arrives after a delete", () => { const gone = { collections: new Set(["c-gone"]), items: new Set(["i-gone"]), photos: new Set(["p-gone"]) }; it("leaves out deleted items, and items of a deleted collection", () => { const page = [{ id: "i1", collection_id: "c1" }, { id: "i-gone", collection_id: "c1" }, { id: "i2", collection_id: "c-gone" }]; expect(ids(withoutDeleted(page, gone))).toEqual(["i1"]); }); it("leaves out deleted photos, and photos of a deleted item or collection", () => { const page = [ { id: "p1", item_id: "i1", collection_id: "c1" }, { id: "p-gone", item_id: "i1", collection_id: "c1" }, { id: "p2", item_id: "i-gone", collection_id: "c1" }, { id: "p3", item_id: "i3", collection_id: "c-gone" }, ]; expect(ids(withoutDeleted(page, gone))).toEqual(["p1"]); }); it("keeps everything when nothing was deleted", () => { const none = { collections: new Set(), items: new Set(), photos: new Set() }; expect(withoutDeleted([{ id: "i1", collection_id: "c1" }], none)).toHaveLength(1); }); }); describe("cutouts being made somewhere else", () => { const now = Date.parse("2026-01-02T10:10:00Z"); const photos = [ { id: "ours", cutout_status: "pending", cutout_requested_at: asked(1000) }, { id: "theirs", cutout_status: "pending", cutout_requested_at: asked(1000) }, { id: "stale", cutout_status: "pending", cutout_requested_at: asked(PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS + 1) }, { id: "done", cutout_status: "done", cutout_file_id: "f" }, { id: "none", cutout_status: "none" }, ]; const held = new Map([["ours", "x"]]); const stale = photos[2]; it("are the pending rows this tab does not hold, an old one first", () => { expect(pendingElsewhere(photos, held, new Set(), now).map((p) => p.id)).toEqual(["stale", "theirs"]); }); it("include an old request until it has been asked about once, and not after", () => { // The tab slept through someone else's cutout: its copy is old, not failed. expect(needsCheck(stale, held, new Set(), now)).toBe(true); const checked = new Set([holdKey(stale)]); expect(needsCheck(stale, held, checked, now)).toBe(false); expect(pendingElsewhere(photos, held, checked, now).map((p) => p.id)).toEqual(["theirs"]); }); it("ask again when the same photo is taken afresh and goes stale again", () => { const checked = new Set([holdKey(stale)]); const retaken = { ...stale, cutout_requested_at: asked(PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS + 5) }; expect(holdKey(retaken)).not.toBe(holdKey(stale)); expect(needsCheck(retaken, held, checked, now)).toBe(true); }); it("never count a fresh request, a held one, or a settled one as needing a check", () => { const none = new Set(); expect(needsCheck(photos[1], held, none, now)).toBe(false); expect(needsCheck({ ...stale, id: "ours" }, held, none, now)).toBe(false); expect(needsCheck({ ...stale, cutout_file_id: "f" }, held, none, now)).toBe(false); expect(needsCheck({ ...stale, cutout_status: "failed" }, held, none, now)).toBe(false); }); it("are asked about a batch at a time", () => { const many = Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, i) => ({ id: `p${i}`, cutout_status: "pending", cutout_requested_at: asked(1000) })); expect(pendingElsewhere(many, new Set(), new Set(), now)).toHaveLength(25); expect(pendingElsewhere(many, new Set(), new Set(), now, 3)).toHaveLength(3); }); }); describe("the acquired date", () => { it("is stored as a real day or not at all", () => { expect(cleanDate("2019-12-25")).toBe("2019-12-25"); expect(cleanDate(" 2020-02-29 ")).toBe("2020-02-29"); for (const bad of ["", null, undefined, "2019-02-30", "2019-13-01", "25/12/2019", "2019-12-25T00:00:00Z", "2019-1-5"]) { expect(cleanDate(bad)).toBeNull(); } }); it("reads as the same day in every time zone", () => { expect(formatDate("2019-12-25", "en-GB")).toBe("25 December 2019"); expect(formatDate("2019-01-01", "en-US")).toBe("January 1, 2019"); expect(formatDate(null)).toBe(""); expect(formatDate("nonsense")).toBe(""); }); it("makes an item findable by the year it was acquired", () => { expect(searchableFields({ name: "Barnaby", note: "", acquired_date: "1998-06-01" })).toContain("1998"); expect(searchableFields({ name: "Barnaby", note: "", acquired_date: null })).toEqual(["Barnaby", ""]); }); }); it("plural", () => { expect(plural(1, "item")).toBe("1 item"); expect(plural(0, "item")).toBe("0 items"); expect(plural(2, "match", "matches")).toBe("2 matches"); });

nodes.body_text: import { readFileSync, existsSync } from "fs"; import { fileURLToPath } from "url"; import { dirname, join } from "path"; import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest"; const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)); const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(__dirname, "../manifest.json"), "utf-8")); const VALID_STORAGE = ["kv", "db", "none"]; const VALID_AUDIENCES = ["everyone", "adults", "children"]; describe("manifest.json", () => { it("has required string fields", () => { for (const field of ["id", "name", "version", "description", "entrypoint", "runtime", "icon"]) { expect(manifest[field], `missing field: ${field}`).toBeTruthy(); } }); it("entrypoint is index.html", () => expect(manifest.entrypoint).toBe("index.html")); it("runtime is static", () => expect(manifest.runtime).toBe("static")); it("storage is declared and valid", () => { expect(manifest.storage, "storage field is required").toBeTruthy(); expect(VALID_STORAGE).toContain(manifest.storage); }); it("version follows semver", () => expect(manifest.version).toMatch(/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/)); it("permissions.default_audience is valid", () => { expect(VALID_AUDIENCES).toContain(manifest.permissions.default_audience); }); it("permissions.requires_approval is boolean", () => { expect(typeof manifest.permissions.requires_approval).toBe("boolean"); }); it("data_access has reads and writes arrays", () => { expect(Array.isArray(manifest.data_access.reads)).toBe(true); expect(Array.isArray(manifest.data_access.writes)).toBe(true); }); }); // ── ai_access SQL file validation ───────────────────────────────────────────── // Auto-discovers all db_exports/db_mutations/db_inserts/db_deletes entries and // validates each SQL file for statement type and single-statement (no semicolons, // which is exactly what the hub enforces). There is no household_id filter to // check — each household is its own D1 database. if (manifest.ai_access) { const ai = manifest.ai_access; const SQL_TYPES = [ { field: "db_exports", dir: "queries", keyword: /^(SELECT|WITH)\b/i, label: "SELECT or WITH" }, { field: "db_mutations", dir: "mutations", keyword: /^UPDATE\b/i, label: "UPDATE" }, { field: "db_inserts", dir: "inserts", keyword: /^INSERT\b/i, label: "INSERT" }, { field: "db_deletes", dir: "deletes", keyword: /^DELETE\b/i, label: "DELETE" }, ]; for (const { field, dir, keyword, label } of SQL_TYPES) { const names = ai[field] ?? []; if (names.length === 0) continue; describe(`ai_access.${field}`, () => { it(`each name has a src/${dir}/{name}.sql file`, () => { for (const name of names) { const path = join(__dirname, `../src/${dir}/${name}.sql`); expect(existsSync(path), `missing: src/${dir}/${name}.sql`).toBe(true); } }); it(`each SQL file starts with ${label}`, () => { for (const name of names) { const path = join(__dirname, `../src/${dir}/${name}.sql`); if (!existsSync(path)) continue; const sql = readFileSync(path, "utf-8").trim(); expect( keyword.test(sql), `src/${dir}/${name}.sql must start with ${label}, got: ${sql.slice(0, 50)}` ).toBe(true); } }); it(`each SQL file is a single statement (no semicolons)`, () => { for (const name of names) { const path = join(__dirname, `../src/${dir}/${name}.sql`); if (!existsSync(path)) continue; const sql = readFileSync(path, "utf-8"); expect( sql.includes(";"), `src/${dir}/${name}.sql must not contain semicolons` ).toBe(false); } }); }); } if (ai.db_inserts?.length) { describe("ai_access.db_inserts schemas", () => { it("each insert has a src/schemas/{name}.json file", () => { for (const name of ai.db_inserts) { const path = join(__dirname, `../src/schemas/${name}.json`); expect(existsSync(path), `missing: src/schemas/${name}.json`).toBe(true); } }); it("each schema file is valid JSON", () => { for (const name of ai.db_inserts) { const path = join(__dirname, `../src/schemas/${name}.json`); if (!existsSync(path)) continue; expect( () => JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf-8")), `src/schemas/${name}.json must be valid JSON` ).not.toThrow(); } }); it("each schema declares type:array with an items definition", () => { for (const name of ai.db_inserts) { const path = join(__dirname, `../src/schemas/${name}.json`); if (!existsSync(path)) continue; let schema; try { schema = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, "utf-8")); } catch { continue; } expect(schema.type, `src/schemas/${name}.json must declare "type": "array"`).toBe("array"); expect( Array.isArray(schema.items) || (typeof schema.items === "object" && schema.items !== null), `src/schemas/${name}.json must declare "items" to validate params` ).toBe(true); } }); it("schema maxItems matches the number of $N placeholders in the SQL", () => { for (const name of ai.db_inserts) { const sqlPath = join(__dirname, `../src/inserts/${name}.sql`); const schemaPath = join(__dirname, `../src/schemas/${name}.json`); if (!existsSync(sqlPath) || !existsSync(schemaPath)) continue; const sql = readFileSync(sqlPath, "utf-8"); let schema; try { schema = JSON.parse(readFileSync(schemaPath, "utf-8")); } catch { continue; } const paramNums = [...sql.matchAll(/\$(\d+)/g)].map(m => parseInt(m[1], 10)); const maxParam = paramNums.length > 0 ? Math.max(...paramNums) : 0; expect( schema.maxItems, `src/schemas/${name}.json maxItems (${schema.maxItems}) must equal SQL $N count (${maxParam})` ).toBe(maxParam); } }); }); } }

A drifted copy is not an error anywhere: it is a preload that // silently never answers. The app posts src/reads.js, so the manifest is held // to that. describe("manifest.preload mirrors the first-render batch", () => { it("declares exactly the statements the app posts, in the order it posts them", () => { expect(Object.keys(preload)).toEqual(READ_ORDER); expect(Object.values(preload).map(({ sql }) => sql)).toEqual(firstRenderBatch().map(({ sql }) => sql)); }); it("stays within the hub's caps and reads only this app's tables", () => { expect(Object.keys(preload).length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(6); for (const [name, { sql, params = [] }] of Object.entries(preload)) { expect(sql, name).toMatch(/^(SELECT|WITH) /); expect(sql, name).not.toMatch(/;|--/); for (const table of sql.match(/(?:FROM|JOIN)\s+(\w+)/g) ?? []) expect(table, name).toMatch(new RegExp(`\\s${prefix}`)); expect((sql.match(/\?/g) ?? []).length, `${name}: placeholders vs params`).toBe(params.length); } }); }); // Every table is governed, and the hub refuses a governed statement whose shape // it cannot rewrite. Nothing in this repo can check that; scenarios.json can, // because the hub replays it against the real runtime. describe("statements the app sends", () => { it("reads are each replayed in scenarios.json, byte for byte", () => { for (const [name, sql] of [...Object.entries(READS), ...Object.entries(NEXT_PAGE)]) { expect(replayed.has(sql), `${name} is not a db step in scenarios.json`).toBe(true); } }); it("fixed statements in index.html are each replayed too", () => { const fixed = [...html.matchAll(/"((?:INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|SELECT) [^"]*app_collections__[^"]*)"/g)].map((m) => m[1]); expect(fixed.length).toBeGreaterThan(8); for (const sql of fixed) expect(replayed.has(sql), `not replayed: ${sql}`).toBe(true); }); // A statement assembled at run time has no text to replay, so the check // above would pass without it. Every statement is spelled out instead. it("none is assembled from a template", () => { const templated = [...html.matchAll(/`\s*(?:INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|SELECT)\b[^`]*`/g)].map((m) => m[0]); expect(templated).toEqual([]); }); }); describe("paging", () => { it("names batch results in the order they were sent", () => { const named = namedResults(READ_ORDER.map((name) => ({ rows: [{ name }] }))); for (const name of READ_ORDER) expect(named[name]).toEqual([{ name }]); expect(namedResults(undefined).items).toEqual([]); }); it("asks for another page only after a full one, starting after its last row", () => { expect(nextPageParams([], FIRST_PAGE_SIZE)).toBeNull(); expect(nextPageParams(page(FIRST_PAGE_SIZE - 1), FIRST_PAGE_SIZE)).toBeNull(); const full = page(FIRST_PAGE_SIZE); const last = full[FIRST_PAGE_SIZE - 1]; expect(nextPageParams(full, FIRST_PAGE_SIZE)).toEqual([last.created_at, last.created_at, last.id]); // The same rows are a short page when more were asked for. expect(nextPageParams(full, NEXT_PAGE_SIZE)).toBeNull(); for (const sql of Object.values(NEXT_PAGE)) expect((sql.match(/\?/g) ?? []).length).toBe(3); }); it("reads the next page of every table that has one in a single batch", () => { const full = page(FIRST_PAGE_SIZE); const short = [row(1)]; expect(nextPageBatch({ items: full, photos: full }, FIRST_PAGE_SIZE).map((s) => s.name)).toEqual(["items", "photos"]); expect(nextPageBatch({ items: short, photos: full }, FIRST_PAGE_SIZE)) .toEqual([{ name: "photos", sql: NEXT_PAGE.photos, params: [full.at(-1).created_at, full.at(-1).created_at, full.at(-1).id] }]); expect(nextPageBatch({ items: short, photos: [] }, FIRST_PAGE_SIZE)).toEqual([]); expect(nextPageBatch({}, NEXT_PAGE_SIZE)).toEqual([]); }); it("asks each statement for the size its page is judged by", () => { for (const name of ["items", "photos"]) expect(READS[name].endsWith(` LIMIT ${FIRST_PAGE_SIZE}`), name).toBe(true); for (const sql of Object.values(NEXT_PAGE)) expect(sql.endsWith(` LIMIT ${NEXT_PAGE_SIZE}`)).toBe(true); }); it("keeps both first pages inside the preload the hub will embed", () => { // Real-shaped rows: every id a UUID, a photo with its thumbnail and cutout, // an item with four tags, two places and a 500-character note, which is // far more than most will carry. Over 256 KB the hub drops the whole // preload and every launch pays for the request again. const uuid = "6082ba46-bf70-4a1a-b4c7-337679bef918"; const at = "2026-10-09T23:11:04.912Z"; const photo = { id: uuid, collection_id: uuid, item_id: uuid, file_id: uuid, thumb_file_id: uuid, cutout_file_id: uuid, cutout_status: "pending", cutout_requested_at: at, use_cutout: 1, sort_order: 12, created_by: uuid, created_at: at }; const item = { id: uuid, collection_id: uuid, name: "n".repeat(40), note: "n".repeat(500), tag_ids: JSON.stringify([uuid, uuid, uuid, uuid]), location_ids: JSON.stringify([uuid, uuid]), created_by: uuid, created_at: at, updated_at: at }; const firstPages = FIRST_PAGE_SIZE * (JSON.stringify(photo).length + JSON.stringify(item).length); // The other three reads share the budget; leave them a quarter of it. expect(firstPages).toBeLessThan(256 * 1024 * 0.75); }); it("stays under the rows one request may return", () => { expect(Object.keys(NEXT_PAGE).length * NEXT_PAGE_SIZE).toBeLessThanOrEqual(5000); }); it("pages carry the same columns and order as the first page", () => { for (const name of Object.keys(NEXT_PAGE)) { expect(head(NEXT_PAGE[name])).toBe(head(READS[name])); expect(tail(NEXT_PAGE[name])).toBe(tail(READS[name])); } }); });

nodes.body_text: /** * Shared migration-schema reader for the manifest ratchets in this suite. * * The manifest names columns the hub resolves in raw SQL — file-reclaim * columns, share-link projections, share-link filters. Every one of those is a * string that no compiler checks, so the tests here re-derive the real column * set from the migrations and compare. */ import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from "fs"; import { fileURLToPath } from "url"; import { dirname, join } from "path"; const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)); export const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(__dirname, "../manifest.json"), "utf-8")); export const prefix = `app_${manifest.id.replaceAll("-", "_")}__`; const migrationsDir = join(__dirname, "../migrations"); export const schema = readdirSync(migrationsDir) .filter((f) => f.endsWith(".sql")) .sort() .map((f) => readFileSync(join(migrationsDir, f), "utf-8")) .join("\n"); /** Every app table's columns: CREATE TABLE bodies plus appended ALTER TABLE ADD * COLUMN statements. Callers need the ALTERs — several columns arrive in a * later migration than the table. */ /** Columns of one UNPREFIXED table name, as the manifest spells it. */ /** Mirrors the hub's `isPlaintextAppDbColumn`: the only columns a raw-SQL * filter (share-link where/parent_where/order) may name. Note the hub does * NOT consult db_encryption here — an app with encryption off still has to * list a non-conventional column in db_plaintext_columns. */ const BUILTIN_PLAINTEXT = new Set([ "id", "household_id", "created_at", "updated_at", "sent_at", "read_at", "expires_at", "last_synced_at", "completed", "all_day", "status", "type", "category", "week", "emoji", "icon", "position", "sort_order", "pinned", "key", "version", "visibility", "audience", "membership_type", "membership_roles", ]);

nodes.name: createTableBody
nodes.body_text: function createTableBody(table) { const head = new RegExp(`create\\s+table\\s+if\\s+not\\s+exists\\s+["\\[]?${table}["\\]]?\\s*\\(`, "i"); const m = head.exec(schema); if (!m) return null; let depth = 1; let i = m.index + m[0].length; const start = i; while (i < schema.length && depth > 0) { if (schema[i] === "(") depth++; else if (schema[i] === ")") depth--; i++; } return schema.slice(start, i - 1); }

nodes.name: columnNames
nodes.body_text: function columnNames(body) { const segments = []; let depth = 0; let current = ""; for (const ch of body) { if (ch === "(") depth++; else if (ch === ")") depth--; if (ch === "," && depth === 0) { segments.push(current); current = ""; } else current += ch; } segments.push(current); const constraints = new Set(["primary", "unique", "check", "foreign", "constraint"]); return segments .map((s) => s.trim()) .filter(Boolean) .map((s) => s.split(/\s+/)[0].replace(/^["[`]|["\]`]$/g, "")) .filter((name) => !constraints.has(name.toLowerCase())); }

nodes.name: appTableColumns
nodes.body_text: function appTableColumns() { const tables = new Map(); for (const m of schema.matchAll(/create\s+table\s+if\s+not\s+exists\s+["\[]?([A-Za-z0-9_]+)["\]]?\s*\(/gi)) { if (!m[1].startsWith(prefix)) continue; const body = createTableBody(m[1]); if (body) tables.set(m[1], new Set(columnNames(body))); } for (const m of schema.matchAll(/alter\s+table\s+["\[]?([A-Za-z0-9_]+)["\]]?\s+add\s+column\s+["\[]?([A-Za-z0-9_]+)["\]]?/gi)) { tables.get(m[1])?.add(m[2]); } return tables; }

nodes.name: columnsOf
nodes.body_text: function columnsOf(table) { return appTableColumns().get(`${prefix}${table}`); }

nodes.name: isPlaintextColumn
nodes.body_text: function isPlaintextColumn(column) { return BUILTIN_PLAINTEXT.has(column) || column.endsWith("_id") || column.endsWith("_at") || column.endsWith("_date") || column.endsWith("_by") || (manifest.db_plaintext_columns ?? []).includes(column); }

nodes.name: build.mjs
nodes.body_text: #!/usr/bin/env node /** * Build script — reads manifest.json + src/ files (+ migrations/ for storage:"db" * apps) and produces dist/bundle.json. * * dist/bundle.json format: * { * "manifest": { ...AppManifest }, * "migrations": [ { "version": 1, "sql": "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ..." }, ... ], * "files": { "index.html": "...", "style.css": "..." } * } * * migrations/ naming convention: * 001_init.sql, 002_add_notes.sql — version is the numeric prefix (no leading zeroes in JSON) * * Upload dist/bundle.json as a GitHub release asset. The hub installs it via * POST /api/apps/install with the release asset URL. */ import fs from "fs"; import path from "path"; const ROOT = new URL(".", import.meta.url).pathname; const SRC = path.join(ROOT, "src"); const DIST = path.join(ROOT, "dist"); // ── Read manifest ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── const manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, "manifest.json"), "utf8")); // ── Read src/ files ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── const files = readDir(SRC); if (!files["index.html"]) { console.error("Error: src/index.html is required"); process.exit(1); } // ── Validate inline scripts parse ───────────────────────────────────────────── // An app's whole UI is one inline `<script type="module">`, and nothing in the // pipeline parses it: the bundle treats src/ as opaque strings, the hub // validates the manifest rather than the markup, and logic.test.mjs never loads // index.html. A duplicate top-level declaration is a SyntaxError the browser // raises before the first statement runs — the app installs, renders its static // markup, and does nothing (tasks 1.5.1: "Identifier 'dbBatch' has already been // declared"). So every inline script is parsed here, the way the browser will, // and duplicate top-level declarations are named explicitly. { const { execFileSync } = await import("child_process"); const os = await import("os"); const errs = []; const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "inline-scripts-")); let count = 0; try { for (const [name, html] of Object.entries(files)) { if (!name.endsWith(".html")) continue; for (const [, attrs = "", body] of html.matchAll(/<script(\s[^>]*)?>([\s\S]*?)<\/script>/g)) { // External scripts and non-JS types (JSON, templates) are not compiled as JS. if (!body.trim() || /\bsrc\s*=/.test(attrs) || /\btype\s*=\s*"(?!module")/.test(attrs)) continue; count++; const isModule = /\btype\s*=\s*"module"/.test(attrs); const file = path.join(dir, `${count}.${isModule ? "mjs" : "cjs"}`); fs.writeFileSync(file, body); try { execFileSync(process.execPath, ["--check", file], { stdio: "pipe" }); } catch (e) { const detail = String(e.stderr ?? e.message).trim().split("\n").filter(Boolean).slice(0, 3).join(" | "); errs.push(`${name}: inline script does not parse — ${detail}`); } const decls = [...body.matchAll(/^(?:async\s+)?function\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)|^(?:const|let|class)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/gm)] .map((m) => m[1] ?? m[2]); const seen = new Set(); for (const decl of decls) { if (seen.has(decl)) errs.push(`${name}: top-level "${decl}" is declared more than once`); seen.add(decl); } } } } finally { fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); } if (errs.length > 0) { for (const e of errs) console.error(`Error: ${e}`); process.exit(1); } console.log(`Inline scripts: ${count} parsed ✓`); } // ── Read + validate migrations (storage:"db" apps only) ─────────────────────── const MIGRATIONS_DIR = path.join(ROOT, "migrations"); let migrations = []; if (manifest.storage === "db") { if (!fs.existsSync(MIGRATIONS_DIR)) { console.error('Error: storage:"db" apps must have a migrations/ directory'); process.exit(1); } const files_ = fs.readdirSync(MIGRATIONS_DIR).filter(f => f.endsWith(".sql")).sort(); if (files_.length === 0) { console.error("Error: migrations/ must contain at least one .sql file"); process.exit(1); } for (const file of files_) { const match = file.match(/^(\d+)/); if (!match) { console.error(`Error: migration file must start with a number: ${file}`); process.exit(1); } const version = parseInt(match[1], 10); const sql = fs.readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS_DIR, file), "utf8").trim(); migrations.push({ version, sql }); } // Validate SQL contracts const FORBIDDEN = [ [/\bdrop\s+table\b/i, "DROP TABLE is not allowed"], [/\bdrop\s+column\b/i, "DROP COLUMN is not allowed"], [/\brename\s+column\b/i, "RENAME COLUMN is not allowed"], [/\balter\s+table\b[^;]+\brename\s+to\b/i, "RENAME TABLE is not allowed"], [/\btruncate\b/i, "TRUNCATE is not allowed"], ]; for (const m of migrations) { for (const [pattern, msg] of FORBIDDEN) { if (pattern.test(m.sql)) { console.error(`Error: migration v${m.version}: ${msg}`); process.exit(1); } } const isCreate = /^\s*create\s+table\b/i.test(m.sql); if (isCreate) { if (!/\bif\s+not\s+exists\b/i.test(m.sql)) { console.error(`Error: migration v${m.version}: CREATE TABLE must use IF NOT EXISTS`); process.exit(1); } } } const versions = migrations.map(m => m.version); if (new Set(versions).size !== versions.length) { console.error("Error: migration versions must be unique"); process.exit(1); } console.log(`Migrations: ${migrations.length} file(s) validated ✓`); } // ── Validate agenda / glance surfaces ───────────────────────────────────────── // The hub re-validates these at publish time and refuses to install a broken // one, so without a local check the first sign of a typo is a failed install // (or, for a display column, a silently dropped widget). These are the // structural rules only — the hub remains the authority. { const errs = surfaceErrors(manifest); if (errs.length > 0) { for (const e of errs) console.error(`Error: ${e}`); process.exit(1); } if (manifest.agenda || manifest.glance) { const which = [manifest.agenda && "agenda", manifest.glance && "glance"].filter(Boolean).join(" + "); console.log(`Surfaces: ${which} validated ✓`); } } // ── Validate inline event handlers resolve to globals ───────────────────────── // An inline `on*=` attribute is compiled by the browser as a function in GLOBAL // scope. Everything declared inside `<script type="module">` is module-scoped, // so such a handler only resolves if the name was explicitly assigned onto // `window`/`globalThis`. Miss one name out of a bridge block and the app builds, // installs, and renders perfectly — then throws // `ReferenceError: Can't find variable: x` the first time a user touches that // one control. Nothing else in the pipeline can see it: the bundle treats src/ // as opaque strings, the hub validates the manifest rather than the markup, and // logic.test.mjs has no DOM. So it is checked here. { const errs = inlineHandlerErrors(files); if (errs.length > 0) { for (const e of errs) console.error(`Error: ${e}`); process.exit(1); } console.log("Inline handlers: all resolve to globals ✓"); } // ── Read scenarios.json (optional per-app behavioral specs) ─────────────────── // Shipped in the bundle so the hub's nightly app-exercise fan-in can replay // scenarios against the published bundle (see hub INTEGRATION_TESTS.md). let scenarios; const SCENARIOS_FILE = path.join(ROOT, "scenarios.json"); if (fs.existsSync(SCENARIOS_FILE)) { scenarios = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(SCENARIOS_FILE, "utf8")); } // ── Read ui-scenarios.json (optional per-app browser specs) ─────────────────── // Layer 3b: Playwright drives the app's own UI inside the real hub. Shipped in // the bundle so the hub can collect scenarios from a published bundle, not just // from a local app dir (see hub DESIGN-app-ui-scenarios.md). let uiScenarios; const UI_SCENARIOS_FILE = path.join(ROOT, "ui-scenarios.json"); if (fs.existsSync(UI_SCENARIOS_FILE)) { uiScenarios = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(UI_SCENARIOS_FILE, "utf8")); } // ── Write bundle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── const bundle = { manifest, ...(migrations.length ? { migrations } : {}), files, ...(scenarios ? { scenarios } : {}), ...(uiScenarios ? { ui_scenarios: uiScenarios } : {}), }; fs.mkdirSync(DIST, { recursive: true }); fs.writeFileSync(path.join(DIST, "bundle.json"), JSON.stringify(bundle, null, 2), "utf8"); const totalBytes = Object.values(files).reduce((s, v) => s + v.length, 0); console.log(`Built ${Object.keys(files).length} file(s) — ${(totalBytes / 1024).toFixed(1)} KB → dist/bundle.json`);

nodes.body_text: function readDir(dir, base = "") { const files = {}; for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) { const rel = base ? `${base}/${entry.name}` : entry.name; if (entry.isDirectory()) Object.assign(files, readDir(path.join(dir, entry.name), rel)); else files[rel] = fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, entry.name), "utf8"); } return files; }

nodes.body_text: function surfaceErrors(m) { const errs = []; // Output aliases the query actually produces: every explicit `AS name`, plus // bare selected columns, which are their own alias (`SELECT title` yields // "title", `SELECT b.name` yields "name"). const aliasesOf = (q) => { const out = new Set([...q.matchAll(/\bAS\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)/gi)].map(x => x[1])); const sel = /^\s*SELECT\s+([\s\S]*?)\sFROM\s/i.exec(q); if (sel) { let depth = 0, cur = ""; const items = []; for (const ch of sel[1]) { if (ch === "(") depth++; else if (ch === ")") depth--; if (ch === "," && depth === 0) { items.push(cur); cur = ""; } else cur += ch; } items.push(cur); for (const raw of items) { const t = raw.trim(); if (/\bAS\b/i.test(t)) continue; const bare = /^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\.?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)?$/.exec(t); if (bare) out.add(bare[2] ?? bare[1]); } } return out; }; const limitOf = (q) => { const x = /\bLIMIT\s+(\d+)\s*$/i.exec(q.trim()); return x ? parseInt(x[1], 10) : null; }; const checkQuery = (q, where) => { if (typeof q !== "string" || !q.trim()) { errs.push(`${where}.source.query must be a non-empty string`); return false; } if (!/^\s*SELECT\b/i.test(q)) errs.push(`${where}.source.query must be a single SELECT`); if (q.includes(";")) errs.push(`${where}.source.query must not contain a semicolon`); if (/\b(INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|DROP|ALTER|CREATE)\b/i.test(q)) errs.push(`${where}.source.query must be read-only`); return true; }; const agenda = m.agenda; if (agenda && agenda.source?.kind === "sql") { const q = agenda.source.query; if (checkQuery(q, "manifest.agenda")) { const aliases = aliasesOf(q); for (const req of ["title", "when_at"]) { if (!aliases.has(req)) errs.push(`manifest.agenda.source.query must select an "${req}" alias`); } const lim = limitOf(q); if (lim === null) errs.push("manifest.agenda.source.query must end with a LIMIT"); else if (lim < 1 || lim > 20) errs.push(`manifest.agenda.source.query LIMIT must be 1-20 (got ${lim})`); // A day token has to narrow the scan, not just be selected or sorted on. // It counts as filtering if it appears anywhere in the WHERE / JOIN ... ON // region, including nested in a function call -- occasions compares // `event_month = CAST(strftime('%m', :today) AS INTEGER)`. const tokens = [...q.matchAll(/:(today|day_start|day_end)\b/g)].map(x => x[0]); if (tokens.length > 0) { const anchor = /\bWHERE\b|\bON\b/i.exec(q); const filterRegion = anchor ? q.slice(anchor.index).replace(/\bORDER\s+BY\b[\s\S]*$/i, "") : ""; if (!tokens.some(t => filterRegion.includes(t))) { errs.push(`manifest.agenda.source.query uses ${tokens[0]} but never filters on it`); } } } } const glance = m.glance; if (glance && glance.source?.kind === "sql") { const q = glance.source.query; if (checkQuery(q, "manifest.glance")) { const aliases = aliasesOf(q); const d = glance.display ?? {}; const TEMPLATES = { stat: ["value"], list: ["title"], badge: ["count"] }; if (!TEMPLATES[d.template]) { errs.push('manifest.glance.display.template must be "stat", "list", or "badge"'); } else { for (const req of TEMPLATES[d.template]) { if (!d[req]) errs.push(`manifest.glance.display.${req} is required for a ${d.template} glance`); } // Every display field names an output alias of the query. for (const f of ["value", "title", "subtitle", "when", "icon", "owner", "count"]) { if (d[f] !== undefined && !aliases.has(d[f])) { errs.push(`manifest.glance.display.${f} "${d[f]}" is not one of the query's selected columns`); } } const lim = limitOf(q); if (d.template === "list" && lim !== null && lim > 5) { errs.push(`manifest.glance.source.query LIMIT must be at most 5 for a list glance (got ${lim})`); } } if (glance.ambient_card !== undefined && glance.ambient_card !== "countdown") { errs.push('manifest.glance.ambient_card must be "countdown"'); } if (glance.ambient_card === "countdown" && d.template !== "list") { errs.push('manifest.glance.ambient_card "countdown" requires display.template "list"'); } } } return errs; }

nodes.body_text: aliasesOf = (q) => { const out = new Set([...q.matchAll(/\bAS\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)/gi)].map(x => x[1])); const sel = /^\s*SELECT\s+([\s\S]*?)\sFROM\s/i.exec(q); if (sel) { let depth = 0, cur = ""; const items = []; for (const ch of sel[1]) { if (ch === "(") depth++; else if (ch === ")") depth--; if (ch === "," && depth === 0) { items.push(cur); cur = ""; } else cur += ch; } items.push(cur); for (const raw of items) { const t = raw.trim(); if (/\bAS\b/i.test(t)) continue; const bare = /^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\.?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)?$/.exec(t); if (bare) out.add(bare[2] ?? bare[1]); } } return out; }

nodes.body_text: function inlineHandlerErrors(files) { const errs = []; // Names an inline handler may reference without the app declaring them. const AMBIENT = new Set([ "event", "this", "window", "document", "console", "navigator", "location", "history", "alert", "confirm", "prompt", "setTimeout", "setInterval", "clearTimeout", "clearInterval", "fetch", "requestAnimationFrame", "queueMicrotask", "structuredClone", "getComputedStyle", "Number", "String", "Boolean", "Array", "Object", "JSON", "Math", "Date", "RegExp", "Map", "Set", "Promise", "Error", "Symbol", "BigInt", "parseInt", "parseFloat", "isNaN", "isFinite", "encodeURIComponent", "decodeURIComponent", "encodeURI", "decodeURI", // keywords that can precede a `(` and are not calls "if", "for", "while", "switch", "catch", "return", "typeof", "function", "new", "await", "var", ]); // `${...}` is evaluated when the template string is built, in module scope — // it is not part of what the browser compiles as a global handler. const stripInterpolations = (s) => { let out = "", i = 0; while (i < s.length) { if (s[i] === "$" && s[i + 1] === "{") { let depth = 1; i += 2; while (i < s.length && depth > 0) { if (s[i] === "{") depth++; else if (s[i] === "}") depth--; i++; } out += "0"; // placeholder for the interpolated value } else out += s[i++]; } return out; }; // A call can't live inside a string literal (`'var(--accent)'` is not a call). const stripStrings = (s) => s.replace(/'[^']*'/g, "''").replace(/`[^`]*`/g, "``"); // Blank out JS comments so a handler quoted in a comment isn't treated as real // markup. nodes.name: dev.mjs
nodes.body_text: #!/usr/bin/env node /** * Generic local dev server for Chickadee Bandit apps. * * Reads the app ID from manifest.json to construct the correct base path. * * hub-sdk.js is fetched from the deployed hub (its canonical source is * packages/hub-contract/src/hub-sdk.js in the hub repo) on first run and cached * locally as .hub-sdk.js (gitignored). If the cache is older than 24 hours * it is refreshed automatically. Falls back to a stale cache when offline. * * Usage: * node dev.mjs # http://localhost:3001 * PORT=3002 node dev.mjs */ import http from "http"; import fs from "fs"; import path from "path"; import https from "https"; import { fileURLToPath } from "url"; const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)); const PORT = parseInt(process.env.PORT ?? "3001", 10); const CACHE = path.join(__dirname, ".hub-sdk.js"); const SDK_URL = "https://www.chickadeebandit.com/hub-sdk.js"; const MAX_AGE_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 24 hours const manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, "manifest.json"), "utf8")); const APP_BASE = `/run/${manifest.id}/`; const MIME = { ".html": "text/html; charset=utf-8", ".js": "text/javascript; charset=utf-8", ".css": "text/css; charset=utf-8", ".json": "application/json", ".svg": "image/svg+xml", ".png": "image/png", ".ico": "image/x-icon", }; await ensureSdk(); http.createServer((req, res) => { const url = req.url.split("?")[0]; if (url === "/hub-sdk.js") { serve(res, CACHE); return; } const stripped = url.startsWith(APP_BASE) ? url.slice(APP_BASE.length) : url.replace(/^\//, ""); serve(res, path.join(__dirname, "src", stripped === "" ? "index.html" : stripped)); }).listen(PORT, () => { console.log(`App: ${manifest.name} (${manifest.id})`); console.log(`Dev server: http://localhost:${PORT}`); });

nodes.name: mime
nodes.body_text: function mime(filepath) { return MIME[path.extname(filepath).toLowerCase()] ?? "application/octet-stream"; }

nodes.name: serve
nodes.body_text: function serve(res, filepath) { try { const body = fs.readFileSync(filepath); res.writeHead(200, { "Content-Type": mime(filepath) }); res.end(body); } catch { res.writeHead(404, { "Content-Type": "text/plain" }); res.end(`Not found: ${filepath}`); } }

nodes.name: fetchSdk
nodes.body_text: function fetchSdk() { return new Promise((resolve, reject) => { https.get(SDK_URL, res => { if (res.statusCode !== 200) { reject(new Error(`HTTP ${res.statusCode}`)); return; } const chunks = []; res.on("data", c => chunks.push(c)); res.on("end", () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8"))); }).on("error", reject); }); }

nodes.name: ensureSdk
nodes.body_text: async function ensureSdk() { const cacheExists = fs.existsSync(CACHE); const cacheAge = cacheExists ? Date.now() - fs.statSync(CACHE).mtimeMs : Infinity; const needsFetch = !cacheExists || cacheAge > MAX_AGE_MS; if (needsFetch) { process.stdout.write(cacheExists ? "Refreshing hub-sdk.js… " : "Fetching hub-sdk.js… "); try { const src = await fetchSdk(); fs.writeFileSync(CACHE, src, "utf8"); console.log("done."); } catch (e) { if (cacheExists) { console.log(`fetch failed (${e.message}), using cached copy.`); } else { console.error(`\nERROR: Could not fetch hub-sdk.js — ${e.message}`); console.error(` Check your internet connection and try again.\n`); process.exit(1); } } } }

nodes.name: logic.js
nodes.body_text: import { isAdult } from "./shared.js"; export { isAdult }; // ── Who may change what ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * Mirrors the `owner_or_visibility` row policy every table carries: the member * who added a row may change or delete it, and so may an adult. Everyone may * add. A button this hides is one the hub would answer with a 403. */ // ── Tags and locations on an item ──────────────────────────────────────────── /** The ids stored in an item's `tag_ids` / `location_ids` column. */ /** Ids that still name a row. A deleted tag stays in the column until the item * is next saved; it is dropped here so it is never drawn or counted. */ /** A name as two people would agree it is the same one. */ /** The row already carrying this name, so "garage" does not sit beside "Garage". */ // ── Finding items ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * Everything a person might type to find an item: its name and note, and the * names of its tags and the places it is stored. `names` maps a tag or * location id to its name. */ /** * Items in a collection that carry EVERY chosen tag and sit in ANY chosen * location. Tags narrow ("Steiff" and "1950s"); an item is only in one place, * so two locations mean "either". */ /** How many items carry each tag or location id. */ // ── Photos ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** An item's photos in the order they are shown: `sort_order`, then oldest first. */ /** The newest item in a collection that has a photo lends the collection its cover. */ // ── Cutouts ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * How long a `pending` row is believed. The request is made by the tab that * added the photo; if that tab closed before the answer came back, nothing will * ever write one. Past this the row reads as failed and may be asked for again. */ export const PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000; /** * How long a hold this tab has just taken needs no renewing. Nobody else can * take a hold until it is PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS old, so one far younger than that * is still ours, and asking the database to confirm it is a wasted request for * every photo added. A hold that has waited in the queue longer is renewed. */ export const HOLD_FRESH_MS = 60 * 1000; const CUTOUT_STATES = new Set(["none", "pending", "done", "failed", "quota"]); /** Where a photo's cutout stands, as the app should treat it right now. */ /** * Whether asking the hub for a cutout is allowed. Each request the hub accepts * spends one of the household's cutouts for the month, and a second request for * the same photo makes a second file, so a photo that has a cutout or is * waiting for one is never asked about again. */ /** True when the item should be drawn from its cutout, not the photo as taken. */ /** The file to draw. `small` prefers the thumbnail of the photo as taken; a * cutout has no thumbnail and is drawn whole. */ /** * What a refused cutout request means for the photo's row. * * status what is written to `cutout_status` * stop the hub will refuse every request the same way, so stop asking * for the rest of this visit * message what to tell the person, once * * A 429 is two different refusals. With a `limit` in the reply it is the * household's monthly allowance; without one it is the hub's per-minute limit * on file requests, which a retry a little later gets past. */ /** One line under a photo saying where its cutout stands, or "" when there is nothing to say. */ // ── Images ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** The size to draw a picture at so its longest side is at most `max`. Never enlarges. */ // ── Rows deleted while more are still arriving ─────────────────────────────── /** * Rows from a page that arrived late, less the ones deleted in the meantime. * Older items and photos are read behind the first paint, so a page asked for * before a delete can land after it, and adding it whole would bring the * deleted rows back until the next reload. `gone` holds the ids deleted in this * visit: `collections`, `items`, `photos`. A row goes if it was deleted itself * or if the collection or item it belongs to was. */ /** One request for one photo: the row and the stamp of the hold on it. */ /** True when the row itself says a cutout is on its way, whatever its age. */ /** * A `pending` row past its five minutes that the database has not yet been * asked about. Its age alone does not mean it failed: this tab may have been * asleep while another finished the cutout, and what it holds is only its own * old copy. So it is asked about once before it is believed. `checked` holds * the holdKey of every stale request already asked about and found unchanged. */ /** * The photos whose cutout someone else is making, or was: every `pending` row * this tab does not hold that is either still fresh or stale and not yet * checked. Their answer is written by another tab or device, so the only way * to learn it is to ask. At most `max`, the most a batch carries; the stale * ones go first, since they are the ones shown wrongly until asked about. */ // ── Dates ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** A date box's value as it is stored: yyyy-mm-dd for a real day, else null. */ /** "12 March 2019" for a stored date, or "" for none. It is a calendar day, * not an instant, so it reads the same in every time zone. */ // ── Small things ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

nodes.name: canEdit
nodes.body_text: function canEdit(row, me) { if (!row || !me) return false; return row.created_by === me.id || isAdult(me); }

nodes.name: parseIds
nodes.body_text: function parseIds(value) { if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.filter((id) => typeof id === "string"); if (typeof value !== "string" || !value) return []; try { const parsed = JSON.parse(value); return Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed.filter((id) => typeof id === "string") : []; } catch { return []; } }

nodes.name: toggleId
nodes.body_text: function toggleId(ids, id) { return ids.includes(id) ? ids.filter((other) => other !== id) : [...ids, id]; }

nodes.name: liveIds
nodes.body_text: function liveIds(ids, rows) { const known = new Set(rows.map((row) => row.id)); return ids.filter((id) => known.has(id)); }

nodes.name: nameKey
nodes.body_text: function nameKey(name) { return String(name ?? "").trim().replace(/\s+/g, " ").toLowerCase(); }

nodes.name: findByName
nodes.body_text: function findByName(rows, name) { const key = nameKey(name); return key ? rows.find((row) => nameKey(row.name) === key) ?? null : null; }

nodes.name: tagsOf
nodes.body_text: function tagsOf(tags, collectionId) { return tags.filter((tag) => tag.collection_id === collectionId); }

nodes.name: searchableFields
nodes.body_text: function searchableFields(item, names = new Map()) { const labels = [...parseIds(item.tag_ids), ...parseIds(item.location_ids)] .map((id) => names.get(id)) .filter(Boolean); // The year it was acquired, so "1998" finds everything from that year. const year = cleanDate(item.acquired_date)?.slice(0, 4); return [item.name, item.note, ...labels, ...(year ? [year] : [])]; }

nodes.name: filterItems
nodes.signature: function filterItems(items, { collectionId = null, tagIds = [], locationIds = [] } = {})
nodes.body_text: function filterItems(items, { collectionId = null, tagIds = [], locationIds = [] } = {}) { return items.filter((item) => { if (collectionId && item.collection_id !== collectionId) return false; const tags = parseIds(item.tag_ids); if (!tagIds.every((id) => tags.includes(id))) return false; if (!locationIds.length) return true; const locations = parseIds(item.location_ids); return locationIds.some((id) => locations.includes(id)); }); }

nodes.name: countByLabel
nodes.body_text: function countByLabel(items, column) { const counts = new Map(); for (const item of items) { for (const id of parseIds(item[column])) counts.set(id, (counts.get(id) ?? 0) + 1); } return counts; }

nodes.name: photosOf
nodes.body_text: function photosOf(photos, itemId) { return photos .filter((photo) => photo.item_id === itemId) .sort((a, b) => (a.sort_order - b.sort_order) || String(a.created_at).localeCompare(String(b.created_at)) || String(a.id).localeCompare(String(b.id))); }

nodes.name: coverPhoto
nodes.body_text: function coverPhoto(photos, itemId) { return photosOf(photos, itemId)[0] ?? null; }

nodes.name: collectionCover
nodes.body_text: function collectionCover(items, photos, collectionId) { const withPhotos = new Set(photos.map((photo) => photo.item_id)); const item = items.find((candidate) => candidate.collection_id === collectionId && withPhotos.has(candidate.id)); return item ? coverPhoto(photos, item.id) : null; }

nodes.name: holdIsFresh
nodes.body_text: function holdIsFresh(stamp, now = Date.now()) { const taken = Date.parse(stamp ?? ""); return Number.isFinite(taken) && now - taken >= 0 && now - taken < HOLD_FRESH_MS; }

nodes.name: cutoutState
nodes.body_text: function cutoutState(photo, now = Date.now()) { if (photo.cutout_file_id) return "done"; const status = CUTOUT_STATES.has(photo.cutout_status) ? photo.cutout_status : "none"; // "done" with no file is a row whose cutout was reclaimed or never written. if (status === "done") return "failed"; if (status !== "pending") return status; const asked = Date.parse(photo.cutout_requested_at ?? ""); return Number.isFinite(asked) && now - asked < PENDING_TIMEOUT_MS ? "pending" : "failed"; }

nodes.name: canRequestCutout
nodes.body_text: function canRequestCutout(photo, now = Date.now()) { const state = cutoutState(photo, now); return state === "none" || state === "failed" || state === "quota"; }

nodes.name: showsCutout
nodes.body_text: function showsCutout(photo) { return !!photo.cutout_file_id && Number(photo.use_cutout) !== 0; }

nodes.name: displayFileId
nodes.body_text: function displayFileId(photo, { small = false } = {}) { if (showsCutout(photo)) return photo.cutout_file_id; return (small && photo.thumb_file_id) || photo.file_id; }

nodes.name: cutoutFailure
nodes.body_text: function cutoutFailure(status, detail = null) { if (status === 429 && typeof detail?.limit === "number") { return { status: "quota", stop: true, message: `This month's ${detail.limit} photo cutouts are used up. New photos are kept as taken.` }; } if (status === 429) return { status: "failed", stop: false, message: "" }; if (status === 402) { return { status: "none", stop: true, message: "Removing photo backgrounds needs an active plan. Photos are kept as taken." }; } if (status === 403) return { status: "none", stop: true, message: "" }; if (status === 503) { return { status: "failed", stop: true, message: "Removing photo backgrounds is unavailable right now. Photos are kept as taken; try again later." }; } if (status === 413) return { status: "failed", stop: false, message: "That photo is too large to remove the background from." }; return { status: "failed", stop: false, message: "" }; }

nodes.name: cutoutLabel
nodes.body_text: function cutoutLabel(state) { switch (state) { case "pending": return "Removing the background…"; case "failed": return "The background could not be removed."; case "quota": return "This month's cutouts are used up."; default: return ""; } }

nodes.name: fitWithin
nodes.body_text: function fitWithin(width, height, max) { const longest = Math.max(width, height); if (!longest || longest <= max) return { width, height, scaled: false }; const scale = max / longest; return { width: Math.round(width * scale), height: Math.round(height * scale), scaled: true }; }

nodes.name: thumbName
nodes.body_text: function thumbName(filename) { const base = String(filename ?? "").replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "").replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9 _-]/g, "").trim().slice(0, 60); return `thumb-${base || "photo"}.jpg`; }

nodes.name: withoutDeleted
nodes.body_text: function withoutDeleted(rows, gone) { return rows.filter((row) => !gone.items.has(row.id) && !gone.photos.has(row.id) && !gone.collections.has(row.collection_id) && !gone.items.has(row.item_id)); }

nodes.name: holdKey
nodes.body_text: function holdKey(photo) { return `${photo.id}|${photo.cutout_requested_at ?? ""}`; }

nodes.name: unresolved
nodes.body_text: function unresolved(photo) { return !photo.cutout_file_id && photo.cutout_status === "pending"; }

nodes.name: needsCheck
nodes.signature: function needsCheck(photo, heldHere, checked, now = Date.now())
nodes.body_text: function needsCheck(photo, heldHere, checked, now = Date.now()) { return unresolved(photo) && !heldHere.has(photo.id) && cutoutState(photo, now) !== "pending" && !checked.has(holdKey(photo)); }

nodes.name: pendingElsewhere
nodes.signature: function pendingElsewhere(photos, heldHere, checked = new Set(), now = Date.now(), max = 25)
nodes.body_text: function pendingElsewhere(photos, heldHere, checked = new Set(), now = Date.now(), max = 25) { const stale = photos.filter((photo) => needsCheck(photo, heldHere, checked, now)); const fresh = photos.filter((photo) => unresolved(photo) && !heldHere.has(photo.id) && cutoutState(photo, now) === "pending"); return [...stale, ...fresh].slice(0, max); }

nodes.name: cleanDate
nodes.body_text: function cleanDate(value) { const text = String(value ?? "").trim(); const match = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/.exec(text); if (!match) return null; const [year, month, day] = match.slice(1).map(Number); const date = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day)); // Date rolls 31 February over into March; a day that does not exist is not stored. return date.getUTCFullYear() === year && date.getUTCMonth() === month - 1 && date.getUTCDate() === day ? text : null; }

nodes.name: formatDate
nodes.body_text: function formatDate(value, locale = undefined) { const clean = cleanDate(value); if (!clean) return ""; const [year, month, day] = clean.split("-").map(Number); return new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day)) .toLocaleDateString(locale, { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric", timeZone: "UTC" }); }

nodes.name: plural
nodes.body_text: function plural(count, one, many = `${one}s`) { return `${count} ${count === 1 ? one : many}`; }

nodes.name: reads.js
nodes.body_text: // Every SELECT the app sends. The first-render ones are also declared in // manifest.preload, which the hub answers from rows embedded in the document; // __tests__/preload.test.mjs holds the two copies together. /** * Items and photos are read a page at a time, newest first, and the two page * sizes answer to different limits. * * The FIRST page of each is preloaded: the hub embeds the rows in the document * and the app's first request costs nothing. The hub drops a whole preload over * 256 KB, and a photo row is about 500 bytes of JSON and an item row about 420 * before its note, so the first page is small enough that both fit with room * for notes, collections, tags and places. * * Every LATER page travels over the network, where the limit is 5,000 rows a * request across both tables. A large page there means a household with a * thousand photos pays one more request, not eight. */ export const FIRST_PAGE_SIZE = 120; export const NEXT_PAGE_SIZE = 1500; export const READS = { collections: "SELECT id, name, description, auto_cutout, created_by, created_at, updated_at FROM app_collections__collections ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC", tags: "SELECT id, collection_id, name, created_by, created_at FROM app_collections__tags ORDER BY created_at, id", locations: "SELECT id, name, created_by, created_at FROM app_collections__locations ORDER BY created_at, id", items: `SELECT id, collection_id, name, note, acquired_date, tag_ids, location_ids, created_by, created_at, updated_at FROM app_collections__items ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ${FIRST_PAGE_SIZE}`, photos: `SELECT id, collection_id, item_id, file_id, thumb_file_id, cutout_file_id, cutout_status, cutout_requested_at, use_cutout, sort_order, created_by, created_at FROM app_collections__photos ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ${FIRST_PAGE_SIZE}`, }; /** The order of the first-render batch, and of manifest.preload. */ export const READ_ORDER = ["collections", "tags", "locations", "items", "photos"]; // The page after a given row. Same columns and order as the first page, so the // pages concatenate. export const NEXT_PAGE = { items: `SELECT id, collection_id, name, note, acquired_date, tag_ids, location_ids, created_by, created_at, updated_at FROM app_collections__items WHERE (created_at < ? OR (created_at = ? AND id < ?)) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ${NEXT_PAGE_SIZE}`, photos: `SELECT id, collection_id, item_id, file_id, thumb_file_id, cutout_file_id, cutout_status, cutout_requested_at, use_cutout, sort_order, created_by, created_at FROM app_collections__photos WHERE (created_at < ? OR (created_at = ? AND id < ?)) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ${NEXT_PAGE_SIZE}`, }; /** Batch results keyed by read name. A missing result reads as no rows. */ /** * The statements for the next round of pages, given the last page read of each * table and the size that page was asked for. Both tables go in one batch, so * a round is one request however many tables still have rows to come. Empty * when everything has been read. */ /** Params for NEXT_PAGE, or null when `rows`, asked for `pageSize` at a time, was the last page. */

nodes.name: firstRenderBatch
nodes.body_text: function firstRenderBatch() { return READ_ORDER.map((name) => ({ sql: READS[name] })); }

nodes.name: namedResults
nodes.body_text: function namedResults(results) { const named = {}; READ_ORDER.forEach((name, i) => { named[name] = results?.[i]?.rows ?? []; }); return named; }

nodes.name: nextPageBatch
nodes.body_text: function nextPageBatch(lastPages, pageSize) { return Object.keys(NEXT_PAGE) .map((name) => ({ name, sql: NEXT_PAGE[name], params: nextPageParams(lastPages[name] ?? [], pageSize) })) .filter((statement) => statement.params); }

nodes.name: nextPageParams
nodes.body_text: function nextPageParams(rows, pageSize) { if (!rows.length || rows.length < pageSize) return null; const last = rows[rows.length - 1]; return [last.created_at, last.created_at, last.id]; }
